# Pink Oyster Mushroom (*Pleurotus djamor*) Growth Phases

## Overview
The pink oyster mushroom is known for its vibrant coral-pink to salmon-colored caps and rapid growth cycle. Understanding the distinct growth phases helps optimize cultivation conditions at each stage.

---

## Phase 1: Mycelial Colonization (7-21 days)

### Description
After inoculation, white mycelium spreads through the substrate, converting it into a productive growing medium.

### Key Indicators
- White fungal threads visible throughout grain spawn or sawdust blocks
- Substrate fully colonized when no bare spots remain
- No visible mushrooms yet (pinning has not begun)

### Optimal Conditions
| Parameter | Target Range |
|-----------|--------------|
| Temperature | 24-28°C (75-82°F) for optimal colonization |
| Humidity | 60-70% relative humidity |
| CO₂ Levels | <1,000 ppm |
| Light | Dark or very low light |

### Notes
- Pink oyster mycelium is vigorous and fast-growing
- Colonization completes faster at higher temperatures
- Avoid contamination by maintaining sterile technique during inoculation

---

## Phase 2: Pinning (24-72 hours before fruiting)

### Description
Mycelium signals readiness for fruit body formation through environmental triggers. Small pinheads appear on the substrate surface.

### Key Indicators
- White, tiny mushroom primordia (1-3 mm diameter) visible at growing edges or cut surfaces
- Mycelial mat is fully mature and dense
- Surface shows slight cracking as pins emerge

### Triggers for Pinning
| Trigger | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Fresh air exchange | Increases O₂, decreases CO₂ (<1,000 ppm) |
| Humidity drop to 95%+ RH | Stimulates pin formation |
| Light exposure (8-12 hours/day) | Blue/white light preferred |
| Temperature shift | Slight cooling can help initiate pins |

### Notes
- Pink oysters typically need a slight temperature drop from colonization temps
- Ensure adequate CO₂ exchange to avoid "CO₂ poisoning" which prevents pinning
- Multiple flushes possible with proper management (3-5 typical)

---

## Phase 3: Fruiting / Flush Development (7-14 days per flush)

### Description
Pins rapidly expand into mature fruit bodies. This is the harvestable growth phase.

### Key Indicators
| Stage | Appearance & Characteristics |
|-------|------------------------------|
| **Pin elongation** | Pins grow from 2mm to 5cm in 1-3 days |
| **Cap expansion** | Caps flatten and spread, pink color intensifies |
| **Gill development** | Gills darken as spores begin forming |
| **Maturity** | Cap edges curl slightly inward; stem thickens |

### Optimal Conditions During Fruiting
| Parameter | Target Range |
|-----------|--------------|
| Temperature | 20-25°C (68-77°F) — cooler than colonization |
| Humidity | 90-95% RH for active fruiting bodies |
| CO₂ Levels | <1,000 ppm; avoid >1,500 ppm which causes畸形生长 |
| Light | Indirect light (8 hours/day); blue-spectrum beneficial |

### Harvest Timing
Pink oyster mushrooms are best harvested when:
- Cap edges have not fully curled
- Gills show pinkish coloration with darkening spots forming
- Caps remain relatively flat to slightly convex

Harvest by twisting or cutting the stem close to substrate. Wear gloves if you prefer (some find mycelium irritating).

---

## Phase 4: Senescence / Post-Harvest Decay

### Description
After harvest, spent substrates and remaining mushrooms enter decline phase before being recycled into compost.

### Key Indicators
- Caps turn dark brown/black with age
- Spore clouds visible when disturbed (spores are black)
- Mycelium recedes from harvested areas
- Remaining pins may produce another flush if conditions remain optimal

### Substrate Reuse Options
| Method | Viability |
|--------|-----------|
| Second flush harvest | 1-2 additional flushes possible with fresh air/water misting |
| Composting substrate | Return to garden or mushroom compost system |
| Animal feed (with caution) | Check local regulations for spore dispersal concerns |

---

## Summary Timeline

```
Day 0: Inoculation
│
├─ Days 1-7 : Early colonization (mycelium spreading through substrate)
│
├─ Days 8-21: Complete mycelial mat formation
│           ↓
└── Day 24+ : Pinning begins (triggered by environmental shift)
              │
              ├─ Hours 0-72   : Pins emerge and grow to ~5cm
              │
              └─ Days 3-10   : Full flush development → Harvest window

After first harvest:
├── Optional second/third flush with fresh air, misting
└── Then senescence/composting phase
```

---

## Cultivation Tips by Phase

### Colonization Phase
- Keep substrate moist but not waterlogged
- Maintain temperature above 24°C for fastest colonization
- Protect from contamination during this vulnerable period

### Pinning Transition
- Introduce fresh air exchange gradually (open covers)
- Mist to raise humidity, then allow brief lower-humidity interval
- Provide indirect light; avoid direct sunlight which can burn developing pins

### Fruiting Phase
- Maintain high humidity with fine misting every 6-8 hours
- Ensure adequate ventilation without drying out substrate
- Harvest promptly at peak maturity for best quality and shelf life

## Environmental Summary Table

| Growth Stage | Temp (°C) | Humidity (%) | CO₂ ppm | Light Needs | Duration |
|--------------|-----------|--------------|---------|-------------|----------|
| Colonization | 24-28     | 60-70        | Any*    | None/Dark   | 10-21 days |
| Pinning      | 20-25     | 90-95+       | <1,000  | Indirect light (8h) | 3-4 days |
| Fruiting     | 20-25     | 90-95        | <1,000  | Indirect light (8h) | 7-14 days per flush |

\*During colonization CO₂ doesn't matter much; becomes critical for pinning/fruiting.

---

## Troubleshooting Quick Reference

| Issue | Likely Cause | Solution |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| No pins forming (all white) | High CO₂, insufficient fresh air, wrong temperature | Increase ventilation, check temps are 20-25°C for pinning |
| Pins turning yellow/brown quickly | Too dry or too warm during fruiting | Mist more often; cool slightly if overheating |
| Mushrooms not opening (buttoned) | High CO₂ levels >1,500 ppm | Increase airflow significantly |
| Dark/abnormal caps | Temperature shock or inconsistent conditions | Stabilize environment before next flush |
